occasions.recipeTitle: Pomegranate & Ras El Hanout Braised Lamb Shoulder
occasions.cuisine: Middle Eastern · North African · For Two · Scales to 12

swaps.text: butternut squash + chickpeas, same spices, roasted alongside the lamb

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Toss diced squash and drained chickpeas with the same spices as the lamb rub, plus a little oil. Spread on a separate tray.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Slide the tray into the same oven as the lamb, alongside the casserole, for the last 55 minutes of the braise — same shelf if there's room, otherwise the shelf below.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Straight from the oven, no rest needed. Finishes right as the lamb comes out.

swaps.text: salmon, half the ras el hanout, roasted after the lamb comes out

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Pat salmon fillets dry. Rub with half the ras el hanout — the milder spicing lets the fish stay the point, not the spice. Season with salt.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Oven up once the lamb comes out. Roast salmon skin-side down on a lined tray until just cooked through and lightly flaking.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Straight from the oven — salmon doesn't rest like the lamb does. Plate alongside the same couscous, yogurt, and mint.

swaps.text: plain chicken thighs, separate pan, mild braising liquid

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Season chicken thighs plainly — salt and pepper only, no ras el hanout. Keep it separate from the spiced braising liquid.

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Brown thighs in their own pan on the stovetop while the lamb is still braising.

phases.name: Simmer
phases.desc: Add a ladle of the lamb's braising liquid (strained, no whole spices) to keep it mild. Cover, simmer until cooked through.

phases.name: Cook the orzo
phases.desc: In a separate pot, cook the orzo in salted water, or in a second ladle of the same strained braising liquid for extra flavor without the spice. Drain if using water.

phases.name: Rest
phases.desc: Chicken off the heat, loosely covered.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Chicken over the orzo, both moistened with a little extra braising liquid if needed.

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Score the lamb deeply all over. Rub entirely with ras el hanout, olive oil and a generous amount of salt. Let the spice crust set before searing.

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Brown all sides in a heavy casserole over high heat until a deep mahogany crust forms. This is where the flavour lives — don't rush it.

phases.name: Braise
phases.desc: Add aromatics, stock and braising liquid. Cover tight. The house will fill with something extraordinary.

phases.name: Rest
phases.desc: Out of the oven, uncovered. Skim the fat from the braising liquid. Shred coarsely back into the juices with two forks.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Over couscous with cold Greek yogurt, fresh mint, and pomegranate seeds scattered at the last moment. Serve family-style.

pairings: Bold Moroccan Syrah or Côtes du Rhône
Labneh with za'atar & flatbread to start

occasions.recipeTitle: Chipotle Pulled Pork with Quick Pickled Slaw & Warm Tortillas

swaps.text: jackfruit, full chipotle rub, same 4-hour braise

phases.name: Rub
phases.desc: Toss drained jackfruit in the same full-strength chipotle rub as the pork.

phases.name: Braise
phases.desc: Same oven, same temperature as the pork, in a separate covered dish. Jackfruit needs about half the pork's time — start it partway through the pork's cook, timed to finish together.

phases.name: Shred & Build
phases.desc: Shreds easily with two forks, just like the pork. Same station.

swaps.text: chipotle cauliflower steaks, roasted separately

phases.name: Rub
phases.desc: Coat cauliflower steaks in the same chipotle rub, thinned with a little oil.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: This needs much higher heat than the pork's slow-cook oven, so it can't share the oven at the same time. Use a second small oven or toaster oven if you have one, or roast after the pork comes out, once the main oven has come up to temperature. Timed to finish as the pork rests.

phases.name: Shred & Build
phases.desc: Same station, alongside the pulled pork and jackfruit.

swaps.text: plain pulled chicken, separate pot, same station

phases.name: Simmer
phases.desc: Plain chicken thighs in a separate pot on the stovetop, covered in stock or water only — no chipotle, no spices.

phases.name: Shred
phases.desc: Shred with two forks once fully cooked and tender.

phases.name: Build
phases.desc: Same station as the pork — tortillas, cheese only, no sauce.

phases.name: Marinate
phases.desc: Coat the pork shoulder entirely in the chipotle rub. Overnight is ideal — the flavour penetrates deep into the meat and the bark will be extraordinary.

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: High heat, all sides. Build the deep crust that locks in the juices and forms the bark. This is where the flavour compounds.

phases.name: Slow Cook
phases.desc: Stock and vinegar added. Covered tight. The kitchen will smell incredible all day.

phases.name: Quick Slaw
phases.desc: Shred red cabbage thinly. Toss with vinegar, sugar and salt while the pork cooks. Rest at least 1 hour — it only gets better with time.

phases.name: Shred & Build
phases.desc: Pull pork with two forks, return to juices. Set up the build-your-own station and let the room serve itself. It holds 4+ hours.

pairings: Mexican lager, margaritas, or agua fresca
Elote-style corn to start the evening

occasions.recipeTitle: Slow-Cooked Chicken & Leek Pie with Buttered Mash

swaps.text: mushrooms & root veg, same cream sauce

phases.name: Simmer
phases.desc: Sauté mushrooms and root veg, then simmer in a portion of the same cream sauce as the main pie filling.

phases.name: Fill & Top
phases.desc: Into its own small pie dish, topped with the same pastry.

phases.name: Bake
phases.desc: Same oven as the main pie, same shelf if there's room.

phases.name: Rest & Serve
phases.desc: Finishes together with the main pie.

swaps.text: coconut cream, plant butter, vegan pastry

phases.name: Simmer
phases.desc: Sauté mushrooms in plant butter, simmer in coconut cream instead of dairy cream.

phases.name: Fill & Top
phases.desc: Into its own small pie dish, topped with vegan puff pastry.

phases.name: Bake
phases.desc: Same oven, same shelf if there's room.

phases.name: Rest & Serve
phases.desc: Finishes together with the main pie.

swaps.text: potato-topped section, no pastry, side of the dish

phases.name: Simmer
phases.desc: Plain chicken thighs simmered in stock only, no cream sauce.

phases.name: Mash the Topping
phases.desc: Boil and mash potatoes plainly — this replaces the pastry lid.

phases.name: Bake
phases.desc: Chicken in its own dish, potato mash spread on top instead of pastry. Same oven, until the top is lightly golden.

phases.name: Rest & Serve
phases.desc: Finishes together with the main pie.

phases.name: Simmer
phases.desc: Place chicken in stock with leeks, celery, carrots, thyme and bay. Simmer gently until tender. Lift out the chicken and shred the meat from the bone.

phases.name: Make the Sauce
phases.desc: Melt butter in a wide pan. Add flour, cook briefly. Pour in the strained cooking stock and cream. Stir until thick, smooth and deeply savoury.

phases.name: Fill & Top
phases.desc: Fold shredded chicken through the leek sauce. Pour into a baking dish. Top with pastry, crimp edges, egg wash generously, pierce to vent.

phases.name: Bake
phases.desc: Until the pastry is deeply golden and filling is bubbling at the edges. It should look beautiful with very little effort on your part. 180°C / 355°F

phases.name: Rest & Serve
phases.desc: Rest 10 minutes before cutting. Serve at the table with buttered mash and peas. Quiet, generous, entirely uncomplicated.

pairings: Strong tea, warm cider, or a good red wine
Green salad, dressed simply with vinegar

occasions.recipeTitle: Honey & Clementine Glazed Ham with Roast Potatoes & Red Cabbage

swaps.text: glazed cauliflower crown, same glaze, roasted alongside the ham

phases.name: Glaze
phases.desc: Brush cauliflower crowns with the same honey and clementine glaze as the ham.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Same oven as the ham's Roast & Lacquer step — the temperature matches exactly, so they can go in together.

phases.name: Carve & Serve
phases.desc: Finishes together with the ham.

swaps.text: whole baked salmon with dill and lemon cream

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Season salmon with dill, lemon, salt. Wrap loosely in foil.

phases.name: Bake
phases.desc: Same oven as the ham, on a lower shelf — salmon needs less time, so add it partway through the ham's roasting step.

phases.name: Lemon Cream
phases.desc: Warm double cream with lemon zest and dill while the salmon rests briefly.

phases.name: Carve & Serve
phases.desc: Finishes together with the ham.

swaps.text: glazed beetroot & lentil Wellington, same table

phases.name: Filling
phases.desc: Mix beetroot and lentils with a little of the ham's glaze for sweetness.

phases.name: Wrap
phases.desc: Wrap the filling in vegan puff pastry.

phases.name: Bake
phases.desc: A little hotter than the ham's oven — bake separately, timed to come out as the ham finishes resting.

phases.name: Carve & Serve
phases.desc: Sliced at the table, same as the ham.

phases.name: Simmer the Ham
phases.desc: Cover gammon in cold water with bay leaves, onion and peppercorns. Bring to boil, reduce and simmer. This draws out excess salt and starts the tenderness.

phases.name: Glaze
phases.desc: Score the fat in a diamond pattern. Stud each diamond with a clove. Mix honey, clementine, mustard and sugar. Coat every surface generously.

phases.name: Roast & Lacquer
phases.desc: High heat to burnish and caramelise the glaze. Baste twice. The ham should emerge glossy, fragrant and deeply golden. 190°C / 375°F

phases.name: Rest
phases.desc: Cover loosely with foil. The resting is non-negotiable — it makes the ham carveable and keeps every slice juicy and intact at the table.

phases.name: Carve & Serve
phases.desc: Serve on a board at the table. The drama of carving is part of the occasion. Cold slices the next day in white rolls with English mustard are the point.

pairings: Good Burgundy or spiced mulled wine
Cheese board and crackers afterwards

occasions.recipeTitle: Build-Your-Own Mini Sliders with Secret Sauce & Oven Fries

swaps.text: black bean & sweetcorn patties, same spices

phases.name: Season & Form
phases.desc: Mash black beans and sweetcorn with the same seasoning as the beef patties, form into equal-sized patties.

phases.name: Cook the Patties
phases.desc: Pan-fry until crisp on both sides — same pan or grill as the beef, cooked separately.

phases.name: Build the Station
phases.desc: Same buns, same station as the beef sliders.

swaps.text: portobello mushroom, soy & smoked paprika marinade

phases.name: Marinate
phases.desc: Soak portobello caps in soy sauce and smoked paprika.

phases.name: Cook
phases.desc: Grill or pan-fry until tender, same station as the beef, cooked separately.

phases.name: Build the Station
phases.desc: Same buns, no cheese unless a vegan slice is available.

swaps.text: plain beef, no seasoning, cheese only, separate pile

phases.name: Form
phases.desc: Form plain patties — no garlic powder, no seasoning at all.

phases.name: Cook the Patties
phases.desc: Pan-fry or grill, same as the main patties but kept in a separate pile.

phases.name: Build the Station
phases.desc: Bun, plain patty, cheese only — no sauce, no toppings.

phases.name: Season & Form
phases.desc: Mix beef with garlic powder, smoked paprika and salt. Form into small patties around 60g each. Keep cold until you cook them — they hold their shape better.

phases.name: Secret Sauce
phases.desc: Mix ketchup, mayonnaise, mustard, and a splash of gherkin brine. That is it. That is the secret. Make twice as much as you think you need.

phases.name: Roast the Fries
phases.desc: Cut potatoes into thin chips. Toss in oil and salt. Spread on trays in a single layer. Roast until golden, crisp, and irresistible. 200°C / 390°F

phases.name: Cook the Patties
phases.desc: Hot pan, 3–4 minutes each side. Add cheese for the final minute and cover with a lid. Cook in batches and keep warm in a low oven.

phases.name: Build the Station
phases.desc: Set up the build-your-own station. Warm the buns first. Let the children assemble their own — the food becomes the activity. Embrace the chaos.

pairings: Homemade milkshakes or fresh fruit smoothies
Birthday cake arrives separately, to cheers

occasions.recipeTitle: Golden Mezze Board: Whipped Feta, Hummus, Warm Flatbreads & Falafel

swaps.text: the entire spread is already plant-based
replace flatbreads with crudités

phases.name: Cut Crudités
phases.desc: Cut cucumber and peppers into dipping sticks for these guests — no separate cooking needed.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Set aside a share of flatbreads equal to this count and swap it for the crudités when assembling the board — same hummus, feta and falafel.

swaps.text: sunflower seed butter instead of tahini

ingredients.name: Sunflower seed butter (in place of tahini)

phases.name: Make a Separate Batch
phases.desc: Whip a small separate portion of hummus using sunflower seed butter instead of tahini, scaled to this count. Also double-check the falafel recipe itself for sesame — most are seed-free, but confirm before serving.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Label this portion clearly, since it's easy to mix up with the regular hummus once plated.

phases.name: Make the Hummus
phases.desc: Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon, garlic and ice-cold water until impossibly smooth. Season very aggressively — hummus wants more salt than you think.

phases.name: Whip the Feta
phases.desc: Blend feta with Greek yogurt and a squeeze of lemon until silky and spreadable. Top with good olive oil and za'atar just before serving.

phases.name: Prep the Vegetables
phases.desc: Halve cherry tomatoes. Slice cucumber into batons. Tear herbs loosely. Arrange everything in natural clusters — not rows. This is the difference between good and great.

phases.name: Char the Breads
phases.desc: Directly over a gas flame or in a very dry hot pan. The char is not an accident — it adds smokiness and warmth that elevates everything else on the board.

phases.name: Assemble the Board
phases.desc: Arrange dips, vegetables, and breads on large boards or trays. Pour olive oil generously over everything. Scatter za'atar. The board arrives, and people feel immediately cared for.

pairings: Dry rosé, gin & tonic, or pomegranate spritz
Add warm marinated olives as a second board

occasions.recipeTitle: Sticky Tamarind & Honey BBQ Chicken with Charred Corn & Herb Slaw

swaps.text: aubergine & halloumi, same glaze, 20 min BBQ

phases.name: Glaze
phases.desc: Brush aubergine slices and halloumi with the same tamarind and honey glaze as the chicken.

phases.name: Grill
phases.desc: Same BBQ or grill pan as the chicken, alongside it — aubergine and halloumi char beautifully at the same heat.

phases.name: Serve Outdoors
phases.desc: Finishes together with the chicken.

swaps.text: glazed tofu & tempeh hold the char beautifully

phases.name: Press & Glaze
phases.desc: Press tofu to remove excess water, slice both tofu and tempeh, brush with the same glaze.

phases.name: Grill
phases.desc: Same BBQ or grill pan as the chicken, alongside it.

phases.name: Serve Outdoors
phases.desc: Finishes together with the chicken.

swaps.text: plain grilled chicken in a bread roll, ketchup on the side, separate plate

phases.name: Grill
phases.desc: Plain chicken thighs, salt only, no marinade — same BBQ, kept on a separate part of the grill.

phases.name: Serve Outdoors
phases.desc: In a bread roll, separate plate, ketchup on the side, no glaze.

phases.name: Marinate
phases.desc: Mix tamarind, honey, soy, garlic, ginger and chilli into a thick paste. Coat chicken thighs entirely. Overnight gives flavour that goes all the way to the bone.

phases.name: BBQ or Oven
phases.desc: On the BBQ over indirect heat, or 200°C in the oven. Baste with remaining marinade halfway through. The glaze caramelises into something smoky and extraordinary. 200°C / 390°F

phases.name: Char the Corn
phases.desc: Directly over the BBQ flame or under a scorching grill. The char is the point — it adds sweetness, smoke, and a visual drama that makes the whole spread sing.

phases.name: Make the Slaw
phases.desc: Shred cabbage and carrot finely. Toss with vinegar, sugar, salt and coriander. The slaw collapses beautifully as the evening progresses and improves with every minute.

phases.name: Serve Outdoors
phases.desc: Pile everything onto large boards. Let people serve themselves. A squeeze of lime over everything at the table is non-negotiable. The garden does the rest.

pairings: Cold lager, Aperol spritz, or fresh lemonade
Jasmine rice or warm naan alongside

occasions.recipeTitle: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Cherry & Port Sauce
occasions.cuisine: French · Romantic · For Two · Scales to 12

swaps.text: roasted beetroot steaks with the same cherry sauce

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Roast beetroots whole, wrapped in foil — start well before the duck, since this takes longer than the duck's whole method combined.

phases.name: Slice
phases.desc: Once cool enough to handle, peel and slice into thick 'steaks.'

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Warm through in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then top with the same cherry and port sauce (made without the duck fat).

swaps.text: pan-seared salmon with dill butter, no port sauce

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Pan-sear salmon skin-side down in its own pan while the duck renders — no need for the oven.

phases.name: Dill Butter
phases.desc: Melt butter with chopped dill and a squeeze of lemon. No port, no duck fat — kept separate.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Salmon topped with dill butter. Timed to finish as the duck rests.

swaps.text: chicken breast, same pan method, sauce made mild

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Same pan method as the duck — skin-side down first to render, then flip.

phases.name: Finish
phases.desc: Finish in the oven alongside the duck, same temperature, until just cooked through.

phases.name: Cook the pasta
phases.desc: Boil tagliatelle in salted water. Toss with a spoon of the pan juices, no port or cherries.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Chicken sliced over the pasta. Timed to finish as the duck rests.

phases.name: Score
phases.desc: Score the duck skin in a diamond pattern, cutting through fat but not flesh. Season generously with salt and rest at room temperature for 20 minutes.

phases.name: Render
phases.desc: Cold pan, skin-side down. Render the fat slowly over medium heat until the skin is deep golden and glass-crisp. This cannot be rushed.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Flip and finish in the oven. Medium-rare: 10 minutes. A thermometer removes all doubt: 54°C internal. 180°C / 355°F

phases.name: Cherry Sauce
phases.desc: Pour off excess fat. Deglaze with port. Add stock, shallots and cherries. Reduce until glossy and coating. Finish with cold butter.

phases.name: Rest & Serve
phases.desc: Rest the duck 8 minutes minimum. Slice on the diagonal against the grain. Sauce pooled on a warm plate. This is the dish.

pairings: Burgundy Pinot Noir or aged Côtes du Rhône
Chicory, walnut and pear salad to start

occasions.recipeTitle: Herb-Crusted Rack of Lamb with Roasted Garlic Mash

swaps.text: baked portobello stack with herb crust, roasted alongside the lamb

phases.name: Herb Crust
phases.desc: Use a portion of the same herb crust mixture — press onto the gill side of each mushroom.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Same oven as the lamb, same shelf if there's room, alongside the racks.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Stack two mushrooms per portion. Finishes together with the lamb.

swaps.text: herb-crusted salmon en croûte, same bake

phases.name: Wrap
phases.desc: Spread a portion of the herb crust mixture over each salmon fillet, wrap in puff pastry.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Same oven as the lamb — pastry should be golden and salmon just cooked through.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Slice thickly. Finishes together with the lamb.

swaps.text: chicken supremes, same herb crust, roasted alongside the lamb

phases.name: Herb Crust
phases.desc: Press a portion of the same herb crust mixture onto the skin side of each chicken supreme.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Same oven, a shelf below the lamb if temperatures need to sit slightly apart.

phases.name: Cook the pasta
phases.desc: Boil tagliatelle in salted water while the chicken roasts. Drain, toss with a little olive oil.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Chicken sliced over the pasta. Finishes together with the lamb.

phases.name: Herb Crust
phases.desc: Blitz breadcrumbs with parsley, rosemary, garlic and olive oil to a vibrant green paste. It should be bright, fragrant and taste like the garden.

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Brown racks on all sides in a very hot pan. Bone side first, then fat side. The colour builds flavour — this step is not optional.

phases.name: Crust & Roast
phases.desc: Coat fat side with Dijon. Press herb crust firmly. Roast until fragrant and deeply golden. Pink inside: non-negotiable. 200°C / 390°F

phases.name: Rest
phases.desc: Cover loosely and leave it completely alone. The lamb continues cooking as it rests. 10 minutes gives you pink. 15 gives you medium.

phases.name: Carve at the Table
phases.desc: Cut into individual cutlets. Stand the racks upright against each other. This is how you make an entrance. This is the graduation.

pairings: A good Bordeaux or Barolo
Pea and fresh mint soup to start

occasions.recipeTitle: Slow-Cooked Beef Bourguignon with Crusty Bread

swaps.text: whole roasted celeriac and root veg, same braising liquid

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Peel celeriac and cut root veg into large chunks — big enough to hold their shape through a long braise.

phases.name: Braise
phases.desc: Add to the oven alongside the beef, in a separate covered dish with a ladle of the same braising liquid. Same oven, same shelf if there's room.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Finishes together with the beef. Serve with the same crusty bread.

swaps.text: monkfish and chorizo stew, same method, less time

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Brown chorizo in its own pan to release its oil, then remove. Sear monkfish briefly in the same pan.

phases.name: Simmer
phases.desc: Return chorizo to the pan with a ladle of the beef's braising liquid. Add monkfish, simmer gently — it cooks fast and toughens if rushed or overdone.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Timed to finish right as the beef comes out to rest. Serve with the same crusty bread.

swaps.text: chicken thighs braised separately, same vegetables and sauce

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Brown chicken thighs in their own pan on the stovetop while the beef is still braising.

phases.name: Braise
phases.desc: Add the same bacon, pearl onions and mushrooms as the main braise, plus a ladle of the beef's braising liquid. Cover, simmer until chicken is tender.

phases.name: Cook the pasta
phases.desc: Boil pappardelle in salted water while the chicken finishes. Drain.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Chicken and sauce over the pappardelle. Timed to finish as the beef comes out to rest.

phases.name: Marinate
phases.desc: Submerge beef in red wine with herbs, garlic and vegetables overnight if possible. The wine tenderises every fibre and deepens every flavour.

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Brown beef in batches over high heat. Every batch needs space. Do not skip this. Dark crust equals deep flavour — this is where the dish is built.

phases.name: Build the Braise
phases.desc: Bacon lardons, pearl onions, mushrooms, the wine marinade, stock. Everything in together. Season generously. This is the whole recipe.

phases.name: Braise
phases.desc: Covered, low and slow. Check once, adjust nothing. The house will smell extraordinary. 150°C / 300°F

phases.name: Rest & Serve
phases.desc: Best made the day before — the flavour deepens overnight. Serve with crusty bread to catch every last drop of the sauce.

pairings: Burgundy Pinot Noir — the same wine as the pot
Simple green salad first, cheese board after

occasions.recipeTitle: Preserved Lemon Roast Chicken with Herbed Couscous & Olives

swaps.text: whole roasted cauliflower, same marinade, roasted alongside the chicken

phases.name: Marinate
phases.desc: Coat whole cauliflowers in the same preserved lemon marinade as the chicken.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Same oven as the chicken, a shelf below if there's room.

phases.name: Serve Family Style
phases.desc: Finishes together with the chicken.

swaps.text: aubergine steaks and chickpeas, same spices, same table

phases.name: Marinate
phases.desc: Coat aubergine steaks and chickpeas in the same preserved lemon marinade.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Same oven as the chicken, a shelf below if there's room.

phases.name: Serve Family Style
phases.desc: Finishes together with the chicken.

swaps.text: plain roasted chicken thighs, no marinade, same couscous

phases.name: Season
phases.desc: Salt only, no marinade.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Same oven, a shelf below the main chicken.

phases.name: Serve Family Style
phases.desc: Alongside the same herbed couscous.

phases.name: Marinate
phases.desc: Rub chickens inside and out with preserved lemon, garlic, cumin and olive oil. Push seasoning under the skin too — loosen it with your fingers.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Olives, onions and lemon pieces arranged around the base. The cooking juices become the sauce. The kitchen fills with something extraordinary. 180°C / 355°F

phases.name: Couscous
phases.desc: Pour boiling stock over couscous and cover tightly. Wait 5 minutes exactly. Fluff with a fork. Add herbs, a squeeze of lemon, a thread of olive oil.

phases.name: Rest
phases.desc: Tent with foil. The skin crisps further. The juices redistribute. The smell deepens. Leave it alone for 15 minutes.

phases.name: Serve Family Style
phases.desc: Bring the whole birds to the table and carve there. The smell is the welcome. It arrives before the food does.

pairings: Dry rosé or a crisp white Viognier
Warm flatbreads and hummus while you wait

occasions.recipeTitle: Individual Beef Wellingtons with Mushroom Duxelles & Red Wine Jus
occasions.cuisine: British · Fine Dining · Special Occasion · Serves 6–16

swaps.text: mushroom, spinach and goat's cheese Wellington, same bake

phases.name: Duxelles
phases.desc: Cook mushrooms and spinach down until dry, exactly like the main duxelles, then cool.

phases.name: Wrap
phases.desc: Layer duxelles and goat's cheese in individual pastry parcels.

phases.name: Bake
phases.desc: Same oven as the beef Wellingtons, same shelf if there's room — no chilling needed first since there's no raw meat inside.

phases.name: Rest & Reveal
phases.desc: Finishes together with the beef.

swaps.text: salmon Wellington with dill cream, baked alongside the beef

phases.name: Wrap
phases.desc: Spread a dill cream over each salmon fillet, wrap individually in puff pastry.

phases.name: Bake
phases.desc: Slightly cooler than the beef Wellingtons — bake on a separate shelf, timed to finish together.

phases.name: Rest & Reveal
phases.desc: Finishes together with the beef.

swaps.text: chicken fillet wrapped in Parma ham and pastry, same bake

phases.name: Wrap
phases.desc: Wrap each chicken fillet in Parma ham, no mushroom duxelles, then in puff pastry.

phases.name: Bake
